newsitem.title: USA: MISSISSIPPI STATE WEEKLY COTTON OUTLOOK - AUG 8.
newsitem.headline: MISSISSIPPI STATE WEEKLY COTTON OUTLOOK - AUG 8.

text.p: Mississippi Cooperative Extension Service. -- August 8, 1997 Weekly Cotton Marketing Advisory Letter. Cotton Market Comments by O.A. Cleveland, Cotton Marketing Specialist:
"The market continues to trade within its year long equilibrium level. Yet, volatility remains an important part of the market.

"While December fell below 74 cents at the week's close, the 77 cent resistance was tested earlier in the week. Thus, the market exhibits every sign of excellent health. Nevertheless, it has been unable to break out of its long standing five to six cent trading range. This trading range appears to be more and more in jeopardy. Long term we favor the higher side of the trading range, but for now, we continue to feel the bottom of the range will be tested.

"We must move through both the August and September reports before the market is able to push above the current 77 cent top. The first objective crop survey of the season will be released Tuesday morning. Remember, the report will reflect conditions as of the last few days in July and the first week of August. It is believed that conditions are deteriorating on a weekly basis. The August estimate will likely approach the 18.4 million bale level. Yet, the widespread belief is that the overall condition of the crop is that it is moving backward. Dryland cut-out is widespread in Texas, the Midsouth and parts of the Southeast. Additionally, fruit set in the Midsouth and Southeast is apparently not as abundant as what had appeared. Without clear sunshine filled days the remainder of August and September the yield reduction will continue into September and early October. Some private estimates carry the 1997 crop as low as 17.5 million bales.

"Certainly, an estimate this low, or even below 18.0 million bales will be viewed as bullish in the marketplace. A crop below 17.9 million bales will open the gates to a breakout above the 77 cent cap now worn by December. Either way, whether the August estimate of the crop is above or below 18.0 million bales, our thought is that additional pricing should be delayed. Patience will be rewarded. However, do not get greedy.

"The international demand for cotton has not slowed. Thus, the supply side of the equation is under pressure to demonstrate that the 1997 crop is out there and can be harvested in a timely manner. Any weakness on the production side will find the market responding in an upward fashion."
